messages.content: What would be the predicted forest growth in the Amazon Rainforest and the Boreal Forests of Canada over the next 10 years and 20 years, respectively, if we do not include the impact of human activities?

function.name: forest_growth_forecast
function.description: Predicts the forest growth over the next N years based on current trends. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location where you want to predict forest growth.

years.description: The number of years for the forecast.

include_human_impact.description: Whether or not to include the impact of human activities in the forecast. If not provided, defaults to false.

message.reasoning: The user wants predictions for two locations: Amazon Rainforest and Boreal Forests of Canada. They want forecasts for 10 years for Amazon and 20 years for Boreal. They explicitly say "if we do not include the impact of human activities". So include_human_impact should be omitted or set to false. The function signature says include_human_impact defaults to false if not provided. So we can omit it. We need to call the function twice: one for Amazon with years=10, one for Boreal with years=20. The user didn't specify a location string exactly; we can use "Amazon Rainforest" and "Boreal Forests of Canada". That matches the location parameter type string. So we will call the function twice.
